questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving, what should you know about braking?

options.text: You can brake only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before the air runs out.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later when convenient.
You must stay at least 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can brake only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. There may be a leak. Your brakes will work only as long as there is enough air left in the tanks.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer, what should you do next?

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Chock the wheels.
Inspect the fifth wheel.
Connect the electrical cord.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Following the correct coupling steps is important for safety. After you connect the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: Why should a driver accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always the best practice.
So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead of you.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on a slippery road can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, what should you never do?

options.text: Push down the brake pedal.
Open the hood.
Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the cab door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never use the brake pedal if spring brakes are activated. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your side door open.
Turn on your emergency flashers.
Wave your arms.
Turn off all your lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When is a vehicle inspection required?

options.text: For insurance purposes.
To get fuel.
By state and federal law.

questions.correctAnswerText: By state and federal law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require that drivers inspect their commercial vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: How does friction form inside a brake drum?

options.text: When brake shoes and linings push against each other.
When brake shoes separate from the axle.
When brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum.
When excess heat is created.

questions.correctAnswerText: When brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction forms when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: How can a driver test coupling?

options.text: By placing their fingers inside the coupling mechanism.
By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
By placing glue over the fifth wheel.
By releasing the orange lever in the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.
questions.explanation: It is important to inspect coupling before starting a trip. You can test coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer.

questions.question: What is true about joggers wearing headsets?

options.text: They are usually aware of what is happening around them.
They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
They can clearly hear traffic sounds.
They usually do not have music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians and joggers wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic and may not know you are there.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck's cab because of what?

options.text: A broken exhaust system.
Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Under-inflated tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: After a trip, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle out of service.
Change the vehicle's oil.
Complete an after-trip inspection of the vehicle.
Disconnect the vehicle's battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete an after-trip inspection of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: After a trip, you may need to inspect the vehicle you drove and file a report about it.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Let you drive faster than normal.
Let you follow other vehicles more closely than normal.
Let you drive less carefully than normal.
Does not reduce your stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not reduce your stopping distance.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you stay in control when braking hard. However, ABS does not shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve do on a truck?

options.text: Add fuel to the vehicle.
Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
Check the oil level.
Load cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch.
Tires should be slightly deflated.
Rear tires need a tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch.
Use a gauge to check that each tire has safe tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires should be slightly deflated.
questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch, and rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Use a gauge to check tread depth. Do not deflate your tires.

questions.question: What is true about doubles and triples?

options.text: They are more stable than straight trucks.
They are most likely to turn over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
They are easier to drive than other vehicles.
They are less affected by wind than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are most likely to turn over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers are more likely to turn over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect. Drivers must steer gently when pulling trailers.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the air supply knob.
Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air using the brake pedal.
Release air using the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air using the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, and pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when pressure drops too low.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does this mean?

options.text: The brakes are working properly.
The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes are new.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, there may be a brake problem. Fix the issue before driving. Operating an unsafe vehicle is illegal.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Continue backing without changing anything.
Pull forward, readjust, and back again.
Get out and move the trailer into position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, readjust, and back again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull forward and reposition your vehicle before continuing to back up.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?

options.text: Red reflective triangles
A flashlight
An electric sign
Tape

questions.correctAnswerText: Red reflective triangles
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes three red reflective triangles, spare fuses, flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.
The front lights will flash.
The vehicle should stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will turn on.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, a low pressure warning signal activates when pressure drops below 60 psi. This signal can be a warning light or a wig wag.
